## Closing {#sec-closing}

### Key Takeaways {#sec-key-takeaways}

- ViTs need large-scale signal; SSL manufactures labels via pretext tasks when manual annotation cannot scale.
- **Joint-embedding** methods (DINO, MoCo) match views; **masked modeling** (MAE, BEiT) reconstructs hidden patches; **JEPA** predicts latent blocks without pixels or augmentations.
- DINO v1 introduced label-free self-distillation with emergent segmentation in [CLS] attention and strong k-NN features on ViT.
- iBOT and DINOv2 combine global DINO + patch iBOT + KoLeo losses; separate projection heads matter at foundation scale.
- DINOv2's LVD-142M pipeline shows curated retrieval beats raw web crawl for frozen feature quality; artifact tokens appear in dense maps (registers mitigate).
- DINOv3 adds Gram anchoring to preserve patch similarity structure during long 7B training; distilled ViT-L models deploy at practical cost.
- Evaluation protocol determines rankings: MAE fine-tunes best; DINO/DINOv2/DINOv3 win frozen linear probe and dense transfer.

### Retrieval Practice {#sec-retrieval-practice}

1. Why does DINO produce segmentation-like attention maps while supervised ViT often does not?
2. What is the fundamental difference between MAE and DINO objectives?
3. Why does DINOv2 combine three losses instead of DINO alone?
4. What problem does Gram anchoring address in DINOv3?
5. When would you choose I-JEPA over DINO?
6. Why does MAE underperform on k-NN but excel after fine-tuning?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answers"}

1. DINO's multi-crop objective forces [CLS] to aggregate semantically consistent regions across local and global views without class labels. Supervised ViT optimizes disease/category logits, not spatial consistency; Objectives Matter shows JE and REC store class information differently ([Shekhar et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13089)).
2. MAE reconstructs masked **pixels** (generative, asymmetric decoder). DINO matches **prototype distributions** across augmented views (discriminative JE). Different targets, different frozen-feature behavior.
3. DINO alone optimizes global [CLS]; dense tasks need patch-level iBOT; KoLeo spreads [CLS] on the sphere for k-NN and stability ([Oquab et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193)).
4. Long training of large models degrades patch similarity maps despite rising global accuracy. Gram anchoring matches student and early-teacher Gram matrices of patch features to preserve dense structure ([Siméoni et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10104)).
5. When augmentations are undesirable or tasks need spatial specificity (depth, counting); I-JEPA predicts latent targets without crop invariance ([Assran et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243)).
6. MAE puts reconstructive detail in patch tokens; [CLS] is weak for global readout until fine-tuning reorganizes information ([Shekhar et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13089); [He et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377)).

:::

### Common Mistakes to Avoid {#sec-common-mistakes}

- **Using k-NN on MAE [CLS] without patch pooling or preprocessing:** distances dominated by high-variance dims; use patch aggregation or fine-tune.
- **Assuming DINOv2/DINOv3 dense maps are artifact-free:** high-norm outlier tokens appear in background; check attention on uniform regions ([Darcet et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16588)).
- **Confusing DeiT with DINO:** DeiT uses supervised CNN teacher; DINO is label-free SSL.
- **Using MAE [CLS] alone for dense prediction:** prefer patch tokens or hybrid models (DINOv2).
- **Skipping data quality when scaling SSL:** DINOv2's LVD-142M curation is load-bearing; raw crawl alone hurts features.

### Curated Resources {#sec-resources}

- [DINO: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14294): original self-distillation method and emergent attention analysis
- [DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193): LVD-142M, hybrid losses, scaling benchmarks
- [DINOv3 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10104): Gram anchoring, 7B training, model family
- [MAE: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06377): 75% masking, asymmetric encoder-decoder
- [iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07832): patch-level online tokenizer
- [I-JEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243): latent predictive SSL without augmentations
- [Objectives Matter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13089): systematic JE vs REC comparison for ViT
- [DINOv3 GitHub](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov3): weights, code, HuggingFace integration
- [Lilian Weng: Self-Supervised Representation Learning](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2019-11-10-self-supervised/): pretext task primer
- [D2L: Transformers for Vision](https://d2l.ai/chapter_attention-mechanisms-and-transformers/vision-transformer.html): ViT architecture tutorial

Maya's arc closes where it opened: unlabeled retinal scans contain structure that class labels alone never taught her supervised ViT. Self-supervised Vision Transformers, from DINO through DINOv3, are the tools that extract that structure and make it usable.
